# Second-pass thesis and evidence audit

**Scope:** `drafts/name-the-if.md`, `drafts/every-if-is-somebodys-when.md`, and
`meta/abundance-transition-programme.md` as read on 2026-09-09.

**Method:** I inventoried the claims in the live documents before reading prior
review reports, then tested material empirical claims against primary or
authoritative sources where feasible. I treated source-supported facts,
inferences, hypotheses, programme rules and value choices as different claim
classes. The audit itself was read-only. No project files were edited during
the audit. This file is a later transcription of its findings.

## Executive verdict

The strongest defensible version of the thesis is:

> **`Verb + scoped outcome + IF` is a proposed grammar for generating,
> challenging and tracking candidate conditions. It is not yet a validated
> method for discovering the true binding condition.**

The public idea is useful. It forces an abundance promise to name the person,
service, standard, place, period, conditions, evidence and decision context that
the promise usually hides. The official healthcare facts mostly survive when
their denominators are kept intact. The programme has also learned several
important distinctions: exposure is not adoption, adoption is not automation,
nominal access is not effective access, a signal is not a warning, and a warning
is not authority.

The central empirical overreach is that the documents sometimes slide from a
useful grammar into a diagnostic claim. No evidence yet shows that the five
prompts discover a complete condition set, that the protocol identifies a
binding condition, that independent users encode the same problem reliably, or
that using the frame improves public understanding or decisions. Those are the
right experiments. They are not current findings.

Four issues are release-blocking:

1. The `$30/$8.30` paragraph reports modelled 2026 distribution estimates as a
   direct observation about people "alive today", calls `$30` a
   "developed-world floor" without a registered basis, and then makes an
   ecological and rhetorical inference that abundance promises address only the
   top fifth. The distribution figures can be retained with their modelled
   status and units. The audience inference must be withdrawn.
2. The phrase "same conditions, different verb" is contradicted by the adjacent
   consumer and provider lists. They are linked but non-identical condition
   registers. The IF/WHEN device can organise questions, but it has not shown
   that the registers are mirrors or that tense identifies an actor's side.
3. The programme calls Australia the "first proof" even though its own source
   triage supports only a prospective, no-consequence feasibility candidate.
4. The programme overstates enforcement. The governance documents explicitly
   say that a caller can bypass the library and that no CI, hosting or operational
   issuance boundary exists. Repository validation can prepare a structurally
   complete candidate packet when invoked. It cannot block publication.

## Verdict key

- **Keep:** supported at the wording and scope stated, or clearly declared as a
  programme rule or value choice.
- **Narrow:** a valid core remains, but the wording exceeds the source,
  denominator, actor, place, period or inference class.
- **Withdraw:** the stated claim is contradicted, materially misleading or not
  recoverable through a small qualification.
- **Unknown:** a meaningful hypothesis for which the required validation has not
  yet been performed.

Priority uses **P0** for a release blocker, **P1** for a material thesis or
decision error, and **P2** for an important communication or precision repair.

| Priority | Location | Material claim | Verdict | Evidence ceiling and required disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | TL;DR, lines 51-54 | Every abundance promise has the shape `verb + blank + IF`. | **Narrow** | This is a proposed analytic rewrite, not an empirical description of every promise. Say "Rewrite an abundance promise as..." or "Many abundance promises become more testable when..." |
| P1 | TL;DR, lines 55-60 | A promise without named conditions cannot be checked, planned around or argued with, and asking for the binding condition turns it into something reportable. | **Narrow / unknown** | Explicit conditions make scope and disagreement more inspectable. They are not strictly necessary for falsifiability, because implicit conditions can be reconstructed. Whether this frame improves reporting is an untested intervention hypothesis. |
| P2 | TL;DR, lines 61-63 | A country is too broad to have one binding IF. | **Keep as a scope rule** | The healthcare sources have incompatible populations, services, dates and units and cannot yield a national binding condition. This does not prove that no national policy constraint could ever dominate a named outcome. |
| P1 | Lines 74-98 | The benchmark shrug is accurate for a mechanical reason; nobody has a life conditional denominated in benchmark performance. | **Withdraw as universal psychology; keep as a hypothesis** | The scene is correctly labelled composite, but "nobody" and the singular causal explanation have no behavioural evidence. Say the benchmark may fail to connect to a person's outcome unless the translation is made explicit, then test that proposition. |
| P0 | Lines 128-132 | Four in five people alive today live below `$30/day`; 44.4% live below `$8.30/day`; `$30` is roughly a developed-world floor; abundance rhetoric therefore speaks almost entirely to the other fifth. | **Narrow the figures; withdraw the inference** | The chart values are modelled global estimates/nowcasts in 2021 international dollars, not direct observations of current people. `$8.30` is the World Bank's June 2025 upper-middle-income poverty line in 2021 PPP. `$30` is a user-set threshold, not an official World Bank poverty line or established developed-world floor. The shares do not identify who hears, makes or can benefit from abundance claims, so the "other fifth" conclusion is an ecological inference and non sequitur. |
| P1 | Lines 138-150 | The frame discriminates between people who name conditions and those who do not; without conditions nobody can be wrong. | **Narrow** | This is argumentative framing. Conditions improve auditability but do not guarantee a proposition is resolvable, and missing explicit conditions do not make all interpretations equally valid. Replace "nobody can be wrong" with "the claim leaves key grounds for disagreement unspecified." |
| P2 | Lines 152-157 | Asking what must be true turns critique into plan; product builders do this instinctively and refuse to do it about the future. | **Withdraw the universal behavioural claim** | The first sentence is a useful posture and value choice. That restraint must control every summary. Completeness, inter-rater reliability, construct validity and decision usefulness remain untested. Until those pass, call this a candidate-condition protocol, not diagnosis. |
| P2 | Lines 186-207 | Price, permission, proximity, availability and capability form a useful starting set; capability is underrated most. | **Keep the prompts; keep the ranking only as an explicit hypothesis** | The draft correctly says this is not a taxonomy and calls the capability example a hypothesis. Preserve that wording. Test omissions and encoder disagreement before claiming coverage. |
| P2 | Lines 204-207 | Continued availability may be reversed on a quarterly earnings call. | **Narrow** | This is plausible for discretionary commercial supply, not for all provision. Public, mutual, regulated, contractual and community systems have different withdrawal mechanisms. |

NCHS: 6.0% of adults aged 18+ failed to obtain needed medical care due to cost in the 2025 NHIS early release. The measures cannot be combined and do not identify a named patient's binding condition. |

Retain "Which condition did this move, for whom?" as a useful editorial question, and test whether readers understand or act differently. |

### Replacement for the poverty paragraph

> World Bank and Our World in Data distribution estimates put about 44.4% of the
> global population below the World Bank's `$8.30/day` upper-middle-income line
> in 2026, expressed in 2021 international dollars. A modelled estimate at a
> user-set `$30/day` threshold puts the share near four in five. These thresholds
> are not income in market US dollars, and `$30` is not an official World Bank
> poverty line. The figures show that affordability conditions are widespread.
> They do not tell us who an abundance promise addresses or which condition
> binds for any person.

If the `$30` result cannot be reproduced directly from a frozen World Bank query
and data vintage, omit it from the public draft and keep the official `$8.30`
line only.

## Claim audit: `Every If Is Somebody's When`

| Priority | Location | Material claim | Verdict | Evidence ceiling and required disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | TL;DR, lines 49-50 | Most abundance promises depend on supply rather than a gift. | **Narrow** | A durable service requires some production and delivery arrangement, but "most" has no defined universe or sample. State the mechanism without a frequency claim. |
| P0 | TL;DR and lines 82-103 | Consumers have IFs, providers have WHENs; these are the same conditions with a different verb, and tense tells which side of the exchange a person occupies. | **Withdraw as stated** | The adjacent examples are not the same list: consumer price, legality and reach differ from model validation, licensing and provider unit cost. They are causally linked but non-identical registers. Actors can simultaneously receive, fund, regulate, deliver and be affected. Tense does not identify a stable actor class. Say "linked conditions, different roles and action hypotheses." |
| P1 | Lines 51-57, 107-120 | The WHEN register belongs in the CEO's view and turns conditions into work. | **Keep as a design proposal, not a discovered rule** | It may be useful for any accountable actor, including workers, service providers, regulators, funders and public bodies. "Belongs" expresses a governance recommendation. A WHEN is correctly limited to a conditional work hypothesis, not a forecast or commitment. |
| P2 | Lines 76-80 | A delivery system has to keep making free healthcare, education or compute available. | **Keep as a logical constraint, narrow the actor language** | Durable access requires continued provision, but provision may be a mixed institutional arrangement rather than a single supplier. Physical, ecological and unmapped constraints may not have a legitimate actor able to move them. |
| P2 | Lines 122-137 | Rewriting free infinite compute as WHEN conditions turns rhetoric into an engineering programme; generosity is not workable. | **Narrow** | The condition list is explicitly illustrative and uncosted. It generates an engineering question, not a programme until service standard, units, dependencies, evidence, costs and authority are specified. Corporate generosity can be one unstable funding route, not the only interpretation of free provision. |
| P1 | Lines 143-166 | Internal process, compliance, review and trust may be an organisational immune response; a parallel organisation can show they were never binding. | **Withdraw as a general diagnosis; retain as competing hypotheses** | The first-person workplace case is not independently verified and the employer is unnamed. Compliance may encode law, contract, safety, insurance or affected-party rights. A parallel team can test whether one route or internal rule was necessary under a bounded scope; it cannot show that the underlying condition was never binding. |
| P1 | Lines 170-193 | Relation mapping is better than one owner field; an external condition cannot be routed around and another party "holds" it. | **Keep the relation map; narrow the impossibility claim** | Control, influence, duty, funding, delivery, dependence, verification and affectedness are usefully separated. An external requirement might be negotiated, satisfied, substituted, challenged or avoided through a different route. "No jurisdiction" is context-specific, not a universal finding. |
| P2 | Lines 195-211 | Some internal preferences can be tested; legal duties, safety boundaries, consent and rights are not business options merely because a firm can afford a penalty. | **Keep as a declared safeguard/value choice** | This is a legitimate normative boundary, not an empirical result. Name who adopted it and how conflicting rights and lawful challenge are handled. "Cost to ignore" must never be treated as authority. |
| P1 | Lines 215-227 | Consumers and providers are asymmetric because the former often have less power. | **Keep as an explicit power hypothesis/value judgement** | The asymmetry is important, but its direction and degree depend on the service and institutions. Define power through observable relations such as authority, outside options, information, bargaining rights, exit and appeal rather than assigning it by actor label. |
| P0 | Lines 229-232 | A public provider does not behave like a company; its WHEN list is a budget cycle and election, not a business case. | **Withdraw** | Publicly financed systems commonly mix public and private delivery, regulated prices, insurers, contracts, professional bodies and user payments. Public bodies also face operations, procurement, liability and business-case-like appraisal; firms can face elections indirectly through law and procurement. Replace the binary with actor-specific financing, authority, delivery and accountability relations. |
| P2 | Lines 248-254 | Abundance occurs when human IFs meet several actors' WHEN hypotheses; a fully internal WHEN list is a mirror, not a plan. | **Keep as thesis synthesis/rhetoric, not evidence** | The synthesis is a proposed governance model. It does not establish necessity, sufficiency or outcome. An internal-only list may sometimes be valid for a bounded internal outcome, so the final line should remain an invitation to test omitted dependencies. |

### Stronger replacement for the IF/WHEN core

> A person's outcome and an actor's delivery plan are not mirror images. They are
> linked condition registers. The public register asks, "Under which conditions
> can this named person achieve this named outcome?" Each actor then records a
> separate work hypothesis: "If these conditions and safeguards hold, what can
> we legitimately act on, prepare for, watch, negotiate, investigate or decline
> to move?" The links between registers must be evidenced. Shared wording does
> not prove a shared condition, and a WHEN does not imply that the outcome will
> arrive.

## Claim audit: `Abundance Transition Programme`

| Priority | Location | Material claim | Verdict | Evidence ceiling and required disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P2 | Lines 22-27 and 42-70 | The mission is to understand when capability becomes shared and durable agency; every project object must expose specified fields. | **Keep as a declared mission and programme rule** | The document correctly says the master proposition is a mission-shaped research question, not a falsifiable empirical claim. The definition of agency and the protected outcomes remain value choices reserved for Fernando and affected participants. |
| P0 | Lines 28-30 | Australia and clerical workers are the "first proof." | **Withdraw "proof"; keep "feasibility candidate"** | Official data provide building blocks, not a closed causal chain or outcome finding. The programme itself later uses "Australian feasibility candidate" and the source triage says it does not support an AI effect, crisis, household-access finding, historical backtest or operational warning. |
| P1 | Lines 31-36 | No signal becomes a warning or action until every transformation is explicit, testable, reversible and owned. | **Keep only as a hard programme policy** | This is a safety requirement, not a verified property of the repository or institution. Some knowledge and communication actions are not literally reversible. Define the covered consequential action class and require evidence that the gate was invoked. |
| P1 | Lines 74-113 | The operating chain and IF/WHEN lens describe the programme's epistemic structure. | **Keep the non-equivalences; narrow the "same conditions" statement** | The listed breaks between capability, reach, use, exposure, adoption, automation, displacement, loss, access, warning, authority and outcome are important anti-inference rules. The consumer and actor registers are linked but non-identical. |
| P1 | Lines 115-144 | Ten non-complacency rules protect the work from unsupported inference and harm. | **Keep as governance commitments** | These are normative and methodological rules, not evidence that compliance occurs. "Every empirical claim" and similar language require automated coverage evidence plus human review; causal alternatives must be relevant to the bounded claim rather than mechanically attached to all observations. |
| P1 | Lines 146-166 | Every material artefact passes seven challenge rounds, and convergence means no unresolved stop-lines or hidden disagreement. | **Narrow to "must pass"** | The programme describes a target process. It does not establish that every current artefact has undergone affected-party, methods, comprehension, operational or independent review. Preserve failed and incomplete states publicly. |
| P1 | Lines 170-218 | Evidence and IF-protocol gates will make public numbers reproducible and permit independent encoders to agree. | **Unknown** | Reproducibility is testable per number. Protocol reliability is not yet measured. Pre-register the claims, encoder instructions, unit of comparison, adjudication rule and an acceptable agreement threshold before the ten-claim test. Do not choose the threshold after results are seen. |
| P0 | Lines 220-246 | The Australia workstream can connect task exposure to work redesign, worker flows, earnings, access and agency. | **Unknown; feasibility only** | NERO, ABS and ILO measure different units and do not close the causal chain. Do not join business AI use, occupational exposure and regional worker outcomes as if they described the same subjects. Each arrow needs a common population/classification or a registered crosswalk, a temporal design, competing explanations and source-independent outcomes. |
| P1 | Lines 248-270 | The forecast programme can score intermediate events, use Brier/log/distributional scores and require improvement over naive baselines. | **Keep as a sound proposed discipline** | Brier and log scores are proper for probabilistic forecasts under their assumptions; continuous targets need proper distributional or quantile scores. This does not establish that the proposed targets are predictable, decision-relevant or sufficiently numerous for calibration claims. Baselines, information floors, vintages, missing outcomes and evaluation windows must be preregistered. |
| P1 | Lines 272-288 | Early-action compacts can distinguish watch, act, pause, reverse, recover and graduate rules. | **Keep as a design proposal, not operational capacity** | Synthetic fixtures can test structure only. They do not create authority, consent, capacity, funding, service levels, appeal or recovery. No public trigger should imply that a real response exists until those institutions are verified and rehearsed. |
| P1 | Lines 290-313 | The public narrative and positive horizon will help readers understand and act appropriately. | **Unknown** | This is a communication intervention hypothesis. "Appropriate" embeds a value judgement and needs a predeclared rubric that permits dissent, refusal and no action. Comprehension, numeracy, anxiety, false certainty, trust and action selection need user studies with affected populations. |
| P2 | Lines 315-329 | The public product must meet WCAG 2.2 AA and pass accessibility, privacy, security and screenshot tests. | **Keep as a requirement** | WCAG 2.2 is an authoritative standard. Conformance cannot be established by schema checks or screenshots alone; combine automated checks with keyboard, screen-reader, zoom/reflow, contrast and user testing. |
| P0 | Lines 331-344 | Governance can ensure that no organisation changes a public conclusion, threshold or forecast without a visible record. | **Unknown and currently unenforced** | This requires an external trusted issuance boundary, authenticated identities, immutable public artefacts and operational control. Repository code cannot enforce it against bypass, alternate hosting or authorised administrators. |
| P1 | Lines 348-369 | The nine priority experiments will validate the proposed system. | **Keep as an experiment backlog; narrow individual claims** | The poverty reconstruction must preserve PPP units and modelled status. The grammar test needs pre-registration. The access test cannot declare a binding condition without full route coverage. The public-instrument trial can test the incremental effect only if facilitation and information are held constant. Ecological materiality needs a declared lifecycle boundary and cannot be inferred from aggregate energy alone. |
| P1 | Lines 371-390 | The checkpoint sequence and external-agent review create a disciplined path to release. | **Keep as process design** | Independent agent agreement is not truth, affected-party participation or professional review. Tags and hashes establish artefact identity only if the referenced bytes and verification process are preserved. |
| P0 | Lines 405-424 | The current checkpoint is Round 02; the repository checks consistency and blocks preparation of an external-review packet until eight categories pass. | **Update stale checkpoint; narrow enforcement claim** | The live branch already contains Round 03 freeze/repair commits. The governance documents say a caller can bypass the library and no CI, hosting or operational issuance boundary exists. At most: "When invoked, the validator rejects a candidate packet whose declared structural fields fail its checks." It cannot block other preparation or publication routes. |
| P0 | Live decision log, line 443 | A machine-readable governance boundary blocks public issuance. | **Withdraw as current-state fact** | `governance/trusted-issuance-boundary.md` says the boundary is missing and the repository cannot authorise a public release. Keep this only as a future design decision: "Require an independently enforced issuance boundary before public release." |
| P1 | Live decision log, line 436 | Australia was chosen because it has "good primary data." | **Narrow** | The sources are credible official building blocks with material limitations. "Good" hides fitness-for-purpose. Say they support a bounded feasibility study but not the causal or lived-outcome chain. |

## Exact primary-source ceilings

These ceilings are the maximum claims the sources support. They are not
instructions to combine the measures.

| Domain | Primary or authoritative source | Exact ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| Global poverty lines | [World Bank, June 2025 update to global poverty lines](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/factsheet/2025/06/05/june-2025-update-to-global-poverty-lines) and [World Bank metadata for the upper-middle-income line](https://databank.worldbank.org/metadataglossary/world-development-indicators/series/SI.POV.UMIC) | In June 2025 the World Bank updated the international poverty lines in 2021 PPP: `$3.00`, `$4.20` and `$8.30` per person per day for international, lower-middle-income and upper-middle-income comparisons. `$30` is not one of these official lines. |
| Global poverty distribution | [World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform](https://pip.worldbank.org/home) and [PIP nowcasts](https://datatopics.worldbank.org/dataviz/pip-nowcasts/) | PIP values may be estimates or nowcasts built from survey distributions, interpolation/extrapolation and macroeconomic inputs. State threshold, PPP vintage, reference year, query date and modelled status. Do not call a user-set threshold a poverty line unless the World Bank does. |
| Processed poverty charts | [Our World in Data `$30/day` chart](https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/poverty-share-on-less-than-30-per-day) and [Our World in Data `$8.30/day` chart](https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/share-living-with-less-than-upper-middle-income-poverty-line) | These pages expose processed World Bank-derived series. The recorded 2026 chart values were about 80.04% below `$30` and 44.38% below `$8.30`, in 2021 international dollars. They are not direct observations, audience measures or individual affordability diagnoses. Freeze the downloadable data and metadata before publication. |
| US insurance | [US Census Bureau, *Health Insurance Coverage in the United States: 2024*](https://www2.census.gov/library/publications/2025/demo/p60-288.pdf) | 27.1 million people, 8.0% of the US population, had no health insurance coverage at any point during calendar year 2024 under CPS ASEC. This does not measure affordability for insured people or access to a named service. |
| US cost-related unmet need | [CDC/NCHS, Access to Health Care](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/fastats/access-to-health-care.htm) | 6.0% of adults aged 18+ failed to obtain needed medical care due to cost in the 2025 NHIS early release. It does not identify the treatment, outcome, causal policy or complete access route. |
| US maternity availability | [HRSA, Maternal Health](https://www.hrsa.gov/maternal-health) | In the cited maternity-care frame, 35% of US counties lacked both an obstetric facility and obstetric providers. This is service-specific and not a measure of all healthcare availability. |
| Spain financing | [Spanish Ministry of Health, common service portfolio](https://www.sanidad.gob.es/profesionales/prestacionesSanitarias/CarteraDeServicios/) | The common basic care portfolio is fully publicly financed. Supplementary services may involve user contributions. This does not support "all healthcare is free." |
| Spain waits | [Spanish Ministry of Health, waiting lists at 31 December 2025](https://www.sanidad.gob.es/estadEstudios/estadisticas/inforRecopilaciones/docs/Informe_situacion_listas_de_espera_dic_2025_V1.pdf) | For registered first hospital specialist consultations at 31 Dec 2025, the patient-weighted mean wait was 102 days and 61.5% of listed patients had an assigned appointment more than 60 days away. It does not establish an individual's wait, care quality or unmet need. |
| Belgium financing | [Belgian FPS Health, invoices and prices](https://www.health.belgium.be/en/themes/health/je-gezondheid/grensoverschrijdende-gezondheidszorg/zorg-het-buitenland/invoices-prices-belgian-healthcare-system) and [Belgian NIHDI/RIZIV, fees, prices and reimbursements](https://www.riziv.fgov.be/fr/themes/soins-de-sante-cout-et-remboursement/les-prestations-de-sante-que-vous-rembourse-votre-mutualite/prestations-de-soins-individuelles/honoraires-prix-et-remboursements) | Recognised care may receive full or partial reimbursement. Contracted providers apply negotiated tariffs with a patient co-payment; non-contracted providers may add supplements. These mechanics do not show the distribution of actual burden or access time. |
| Australia Medicare | [Australian Department of Health, Medicare costs](https://www.health.gov.au/topics/medicare/about/costs) | A bulk-billed service has no patient charge. If a provider does not bulk bill, the patient may pay the difference between the charge and the Medicare benefit. This does not establish appointment availability or universal eligibility. |
| Australia bulk billing | [Australian Department of Health, national GP bulk-billing snapshot](https://www.health.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-02/national-gp-bulk-billing-snapshot-1-november-2025-to-31-january-2026.pdf) | 81.4% of GP non-referred attendance **services** were bulk billed from 1 Nov 2025 through 31 Jan 2026. The denominator is services, not unique patients or people able to obtain a timely appointment. |
| Australia workforce geography | [Australian Department of Health, Distribution Priority Areas](https://www.health.gov.au/topics/rural-health-workforce/classifications/dpa) | The official classification identifies locations with workforce shortages under its rules. It does not establish that any named patient lacks a viable provider or that distance is the binding constraint. |
| Australian regional employment | [Jobs and Skills Australia, NERO](https://www.jobsandskills.gov.au/data/nero) and [NERO methodology](https://www.jobsandskills.gov.au/data/nero/nero-methodology) | NERO supplies monthly **modelled** employment estimates for 355 four-digit occupations across 88 SA4 regions. The series are smoothed, revision-prone, can miss changes outside training history and must not be summed or combined across occupations or geographies. Region is residence, not business location. NERO does not observe causal AI effects. |
| Australian business AI use | [ABS, Characteristics of Australian Business 2024-25](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/industry/technology-and-innovation/characteristics-australian-business/latest-release) | 12% of in-scope businesses reported/select AI use in 2024-25. The statistic is businesses, not workers; it does not measure intensity, tasks, work redesign, local adoption or worker treatment. |
| Occupational exposure | [ILO, refined global index of occupational exposure to generative AI](https://www.ilo.org/publications/generative-ai-and-jobs-refined-global-index-occupational-exposure) | Clerical occupations have the highest modelled potential-exposure classifications in the cited index. Exposure is not observed Australian adoption, automation, displacement, job loss or harm. |
| Product metrics | [Google Research, HEART framework](https://research.google/pubs/measuring-the-user-experience-on-a-large-scale-user-centered-metrics-for-web-applications/) | HEART supports a goals-signals-metrics process for product user experience. It does not validate the IF grammar, a societal-transition model, crisis thresholds or public decision quality. |
| Binary forecast scoring | [Brier, 1950, *Verification of forecasts expressed in terms of probability*](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0493(1950)078%3C0001:VOFEIT%3E2.0.CO;2) | The Brier score evaluates probabilistic forecasts for defined outcomes. A score does not by itself establish calibration, causal validity, usefulness or superiority without a comparator and evaluation design. |
| Proper scoring | [Gneiting and Raftery, 2007, *Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and Estimation*](https://sites.stat.washington.edu/people/raftery/Research/PDF/Gneiting2007jasa.pdf) | Proper scoring rules can evaluate probabilistic distributions or quantiles. Choice of target, score, baseline, sample and decision loss remains part of the registered design. |
| Accessibility | [W3C, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/) | WCAG 2.2 defines testable conformance criteria. Automated checks alone cannot establish full AA conformance or usability for affected people. |
| Ecological inference | [Robinson, 1950, *Ecological Correlations and the Behavior of Individuals*](https://doi.org/10.2307/2087176) | Aggregate relationships cannot be assigned to individuals without a valid design. Business, occupation, region and household statistics must not be interpreted as the treatment, condition or outcome of a named worker. |

## Denominator and inference rules that should become editorial stop-lines

1. Never move from a population share to a claim about the people addressed by
   rhetoric, the constraints faced by an individual, or the beneficiaries of a
   technology without new evidence.
2. Never combine or visually align statistics as though comparable unless
   population, unit, service, place, period, definition and vintage match or the
   crosswalk and its uncertainty are explicit.
3. Never use "people" when the measured unit is services, businesses, jobs,
   counties, appointments or modelled occupation-region cells.
4. Never convert 2021 international dollars into nominal US dollars or compare a
   PPP welfare quantity directly with nominal GDP or company profit.
5. Never turn exposure into adoption, adoption into automation, automation into
   displacement, displacement into lasting loss, or an aggregate change into an
   individual causal effect.
6. Never call a condition binding until all registered viable routes for the
   named person and outcome have been tested, and always state that an
   unregistered route can overturn the conclusion.
7. Never allow a value choice such as "decent life", "amazing abundance",
   "appropriate action", "acceptable agreement" or a loss function to inherit
   the visual status of an empirical finding. Name the chooser and review path.
8. Never describe repository structure, passing tests, a manifest or a hash as
   public authority, affected-party consent, reviewer independence or an
   enforced publication boundary.

## Minimum validation programme before stronger claims

### 1. Validate the grammar before calling it diagnosis

Pre-register ten heterogeneous, real service promises. Give independent
encoders the same bounded evidence without showing them the authors' graphs.
Measure:

- omitted conditions and unsupported additions;
- agreement on scope, logical relation, lifecycle and evidence class;
- sensitivity to the five starting prompts;
- whether affected people identify routes the analysts missed;
- whether different encodings change the action recommendation;
- performance against simpler alternatives, including an ordinary assumptions
  register and causal diagram.

Use the result to narrow the method. Do not revise the agreement threshold after
seeing scores.

### 2. Test the communication intervention

Randomise readers to a conventional release, the same release with explicit
scope and uncertainty, and the full IF presentation. Hold facilitation and
substantive evidence constant. Measure factual comprehension, denominator
recognition, uncertainty calibration, false causal inference, anxiety, trust,
ability to find the owner and appeal route, and a predeclared range of defensible
actions including waiting, dissent and refusal. This distinguishes the value of
good statistical communication from the incremental value of the branded frame.

### 3. Keep Australia prospective and no-consequence

Freeze one NERO vintage, occupation code, SA4, outcome unit and revision policy.
Acquire one source-independent employment or worker-flow outcome and one
independently measured adoption or task-redesign event. Register technology,
macro-demand, sector composition, measurement/reclassification,
policy/ownership and no-material-change graphs. Do not issue a crisis state or
action recommendation from NERO movement alone.

### 4. Separate structural validation from legitimate issuance

Rename all current checks as candidate-packet structural validation. Build the
trusted boundary only after there are authenticated identities, externally
enforced release controls, role separation, immutable artefact publication,
review evidence, revocation/correction procedures and a tested bypass threat
model. Until then, every generated public view should say that the repository
does not authorise publication or action.

## Final disposition

The thesis should continue, but at its current evidence ceiling:

> **A promising public and operational grammar for exposing candidate
> conditions, missing evidence, actor relations and legitimate action posture.**

It should not yet be presented as:

- a validated diagnostic of the true binding condition;
- a complete taxonomy of access or agency;
- evidence that abundance rhetoric addresses only the richest fifth;
- proof that consumer IFs and provider WHENs are the same conditions;
- proof of an Australian AI transition or crisis;
- an authorised warning or early-action system; or
- an enforced public-release governance boundary.

The documents become stronger, not weaker, when they say this plainly. The
honest public promise is not that the Observatory already knows the crossing. It
is that every important inference will expose its IF, every unknown can remain
unknown, every value choice will name its author, and every proposed action can
be challenged before it acquires authority.
